sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Anti-FLAG immunofluorescence confirmed correct subcellular localization of the tagged wild-type protein; no functional assay (e.g., binding, signalling) reported in the cited clips.
sites.rationale: Both L1 and L2 describe the same N-terminally FLAG-tagged full-length KIRREL1 construct used for localization studies. The signal peptide spans residues 1–16 (computed landmarks), so a tag placed 'at the N-terminus' of the mature protein sits after residue 16 (S) and before residue 17 (Q), 480 residues from the TM boundary — well within the extracellular domain. Because the C-terminus is intracellular, this is the sole extracellular terminus and the position is unambiguous by topology. Python confirmed residue_before = S (pos 16) and residue_after = Q (pos 17). PMC6756928 reports full-length KIRREL1 constructs (wild-type and patient mutants) carrying a FLAG tag described as 'at the N-terminus'. The construct is membrane-anchored (not a secreted ectodomain), expressed in cells, and detected by anti-FLAG immunofluorescence microscopy. No specific residue number is named; the paper says only 'N-terminus'. With signal peptide 1–16 and the C-terminus intracellular (519–757), the only extracellular terminus is the mature N-terminus beginning at residue 17, so the tag must follow the signal-peptide cleavage site at residue 16.

sources.claim: To test this hypothesis, we generated cDNA constructs containing patient’s mutant alleles with inserted Flag tag at the N-terminus ( Fig.2A ).

literature_notes: L1 and L2 are two clips from the same paper (PMC6756928) describing the same construct; they ground one site, not two. No residue number is stated, so position_evidence is topology_derived rather than validated. The C-terminus (residues 519–757) is intracellular and therefore not a candidate for a surface tag. No other ledger lines describe internal-loop insertions, transposon screens, or fluorescent-protein fusions in KIRREL1 or close orthologs, so no internal sites are proposed.
